sections.name: Why Your Foot Falls Asleep
lines: Sit on your legs for too long, and your foot goes completely numb.
Your foot isn't asleep. Its nerves are being squashed.
The pressure squeezes the nerve, and the blood vessels that feed it, so its signals slow down, then stop.
Move, and the nerve restarts all at once, firing off random signals.
Your brain reads that static as pins and needles.
A minute or two later, everything's back to normal.
But if it keeps happening for no reason, get it checked by a doctor.
